verses.1: Call out now, is there anyone who answers you? To which of the holy ones will you turn?
verses.2: For a fool is struck down by his anger, and a man of understanding is killed by his jealousy.
verses.3: I have seen a fool planting roots, but suddenly I plucked up his nourishment.
verses.4: His children are driven from safety, and they are crushed in the gate with no one to rescue them.
verses.5: What he has gathered, the hungry will eat, and he will take it to the dry ground, and the thirsty will exhaust his strength.
verses.6: For evil does not come from the dust, and toil does not spring from the soil.
verses.7: For man is born to toil, and the sons of wrath are lifted up like sparks.
verses.8: But I would seek the God who made me and would place my plea before the Almighty.
verses.9: The one who does great things beyond understanding, wonders without number,
verses.10: who pours rain on the earth and sends water on the wilderness,
verses.11: who brings low the lofty and lifts up the lowly, who rescues the oppressed,
verses.12: who breaks the plans of the cunning, so that their hands do no accomplish what is right,
verses.13: who captures the wise in their craftiness, and the counsel of the shrewd is quickly undone,
verses.14: who meets the daylight with darkness, and the noonday feels as though it were night.
verses.15: Who rescues from the sword's mouth and from the hand of the strong, the weak,
verses.16: so that the poor have hope, and the mouth of the wicked is shut.
verses.17: Behold, happy is the man whom God corrects, and do not despise the discipline of the Almighty.
verses.18: For He will strike, yet He will heal; He will wound, yet His hands will restore.
verses.19: He will rescue you from six troubles, and in the seventh, evil will not touch you.
verses.20: In famine, He will deliver you from death, and in war, from the hand of the sword.
verses.21: From the lash of the tongue He will hide you, and you will not fear when evil comes.
verses.22: You will laugh at the outlaw and the lawless, and from the wild beasts of the land you will not fear.
verses.23: For with the stones of the field is your covenant, and the wild beasts of the field will make peace with you.
verses.24: You will know that peace dwells in your tent, and your dwelling place will not be disturbed.
verses.25: You will know that your descendants are numerous, like the grass of the earth.
verses.26: You will come in with a full harvest, like grain brought in at the proper time, like a sheaf of gleaning brought in at its season.
verses.27: Look, we have examined these things; this is the truth we have heard. You, then, know it for yourself.

notes:
Notes
- v. 20: "From the lash of the tongue He will hide you" — the Hebrew "מִשֹּׁט לָשׁוֹן" is rendered as "from the lash of the tongue," reflecting the metaphor of a whip-like tongue.
- v. 23: "with the stones of the field is your covenant" — the Hebrew "כִּי עִם־אַבְנֵי הַשָּׂדֶה בְרִיתֶךָ" is translated to reflect the idea of a covenant secured with the very foundation of the land.
